definitions.explanation: A person whose job is to clean buildings, facilities, streets, or other areas. A formal occupational title.

examples.japanese: {清掃員|せいそういん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{廊下|ろうか}→廊下：05005_rouka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The janitor is cleaning the hallway.

examples.japanese: ⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{清掃員|せいそういん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{募集|ぼしゅう}→募集：03035_boshuu⟧⟦しています→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We are looking for building cleaning staff.

examples.japanese: ⟦{早朝|そうちょう}→早朝：03109_souchou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{清掃員|せいそういん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦きれい→きれい：00717_kirei⟧にして⟦くれている→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: From early morning, the cleaning staff are keeping the area in front of the station clean for us.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{清掃|せいそう}→清掃：04332_seisou⟧ (cleaning) + {員|いん} (member/staff). A formal and respectful occupational title for cleaners.

USAGE:
{清掃員|せいそういん} is the standard, polite way to refer to cleaning workers. It is used in job listings, workplace settings, and official contexts.
The suffix {員|いん} is widely used in Japanese for occupational titles (⟦{会社員|かいしゃいん}→会社員：03018_kaishain⟧, ⟦{公務員|こうむいん}→公務員：01588_koumuin⟧, ⟦{駅員|えきいん}→駅員：05503_ekiin⟧, etc.).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧{清掃員|せいそういん}: building cleaner
- ⟦{道路|どうろ}→道路：01481_douro⟧{清掃員|せいそういん}: street sweeper
- {清掃員|せいそういん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{募集|ぼしゅう}→募集：03035_boshuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to recruit cleaning staff
- {清掃員|せいそういん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to work as a janitor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧{係|がかり}: person in charge of cleaning — less formal, often used for assigned duties at school
- {用務員|ようむいん}: school custodian — handles general maintenance and cleaning at schools
- ⟦{清掃|せいそう}→清掃：04332_seisou⟧⟦{業者|ぎょうしゃ}→業者：13130_gyousha⟧: cleaning company/contractor — refers to the company rather than the individual
